senses.gloss: m. (צָרַף) [narrow,] cone-shaped roof of reeds &c.; cone-shaped hut (v. Sm. Ant.3, Engl, ed., s. v. Tugurium).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 1:11">Succ. I, 11</cite> <he>העושה … כמין צ׳</he> if a man makes his Succah in the shape of a cone (the walls forming the roof); Tosef. ib. I, 10.

<cite ref="Shabbat 56b:15">Sabb. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>אותו היום … נבנה צ׳ וכ׳</he> on the day, when Jeroboam introduced two golden calves …, a hut was built (on the site of Rome), and this grew to be Greek Italy; a. e.—Pl. <he>צְרִיפִים</he>, <he>צְרִיפִין</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:2:8">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᶜ</cite> <he>יום … שני צ׳ ברומי</he> on the day when Jeroboam …, Remus and Romulus came and built two huts on the site of Rome; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6:4">Cant. R. to I, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 3:2">Esth. R. to I, 9</cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 55b:14">Erub. 55ᵇ</cite> <he>יושבי צ׳ כיושבי קברים</he> dwellers in cots are like dwellers in graves.
Ex. R. s. 20 הרס את הצ׳ he destroyed the shepherd’s cots; a. e.—גַגּוֹת צְרִיפִין pr. n. pl. Gaggoth Ts’rifin (Cottage Roofs).

<cite ref="Menachot 64b:2">Ib. 64ᵇ</cite>; Y. Shek. V, 48ᵈ top <he>פעם אחת אית אתר דמתקרי ג׳ צ׳ או צ׳ ג׳ …</he> it once occurred during a drought …, when they did not know whence to get the ʿOmer, that a mute was there, and he put one hand on (pointed to) <he>גגות</he> (flat roofs) and one on <he>צריפין</he> (cone-shaped roofs); they brought him before Pethahiah (Mordecai), who asked, Is there a place called G. Ts. or Ts. G.?
